title: About Nikhil
tags: who are you about yourself introduce background summary nikhil obuleni
sents: Nikhil Obuleni is an AI research engineer in Washington, DC who builds LLM and retrieval systems that run in production.
He builds LLM systems for people who cannot afford a wrong answer: clinicians, counselors, and field teams in low-resource settings.
Most of what he builds runs against real clinical and humanitarian data, so accuracy and traceability matter more than benchmark scores.
His work covers agent pipelines, retrieval systems, evaluation, and the data infrastructure that feeds them.

title: AI Research Engineer · CGMHE (Mar 2026 – now)
tags: now current job role work today employer center for global mental health equity gwu who unicef
sents: Since March 2026 he has been an AI Research Engineer at the Center for Global Mental Health Equity (CGMHE) at GWU, building LLM systems for WHO and UNICEF mental health programs.
He shipped an LLM agent pipeline (LangChain, OpenAI API) that automates counselor competency scoring across 26K+ multilingual clinical transcripts in 25 countries.
That pipeline cut per-session review time from 45 minutes to 4 and replaced a fully manual WHO/UNICEF evaluation process.
He designed a production RAG system (FAISS, LangChain, FastAPI) grounding LLM output in EQUIP/ENACT clinical rubrics, with chunking, reranking, and a hallucination-flagging layer.
The RAG system reduced the factual error rate by roughly 40% on held-out multilingual benchmarks.
He ran LLM evaluation experiments (RAGAS, DeepEval) comparing GPT-4 and Claude against human-annotated ground truth across 14 languages.
The evaluation found a 23% calibration gap on low-resource languages, which fed into a joint OpenAI collaboration on clinical LLM deployment.
He built Airflow and AWS (S3, EC2) pipelines ingesting 500K+ patient records into PostgreSQL across 25+ countries on a $2.9M NIMH grant.
Those pipelines cut integration latency 83% and reporting time 60%.

title: medrag-toolkit
tags: rag retrieval medical question answering pubmed openfda rxnorm grounding citations abstain hybrid
sents: medrag-toolkit is a modular RAG framework for medical question answering with connectors to PubMed (36M+ abstracts), RxNorm, and OpenFDA.
Every medrag-toolkit response enforces citation grounding: each sentence is checked against its source, unsupported sentences are dropped, and it abstains rather than guesses.
It uses hybrid retrieval, combining dense FAISS with sparse BM25 over Qdrant.
A streaming FastAPI layer supports local backends (Ollama, vLLM) as well as cloud LLMs, and it is benchmarked on MedQA and MedMCQA.

title: ragcheck
tags: evaluation eval rag faithfulness hallucination ci gate testing metrics
sents: ragcheck scores retrieval, faithfulness, relevance, and citation coverage separately, and prints the exact sentences a RAG answer made up.
ragcheck has an offline judge for CI, an LLM judge for depth, and a gate command that fails the build.
ragcheck is the open-source distillation of his clinical LLM evaluation work.

title: abtest-kit
tags: ab testing experiments statistics bayesian sequential cuped peeking power analysis
sents: abtest-kit covers power analysis, z and Welch tests, Bayesian expected loss, always-valid sequential tests, and CUPED.
Each abtest-kit method is tested against an independent reference.
In the abtest-kit peeking demo, a naive t-test gives 32% false positives while mSPRT gives 1.8%.

title: PlanMoE
tags: mixture of experts generative floor plan gcn quantization deep learning
sents: PlanMoE is a generative floor plan designer: a custom mixture of experts with a 3-layer GCN encoder and a transposed-convolution mask decoder.
In PlanMoE each expert specializes in one room-type layout, and a learned gating network routes room-constraint graphs to the right expert.
PlanMoE is deployed as a Hugging Face Space, and INT8 post-training quantization cut inference latency 52%.

title: Clinical RAG Evaluation System
tags: rag guidelines who nimh pinecone lambda guardrails prompt injection
sents: The Clinical RAG Evaluation System is a RAG pipeline over 5,000+ WHO and NIMH clinical guidelines, deployed on AWS Lambda behind FastAPI.
It uses LangChain and Pinecone for retrieval, prompt-injection guardrails on the input path, and LangSmith for evaluation logging.
Benchmarked with RAGAS and tested with 3 clinical reviewers, it reached 91% response relevance, 38% fewer hallucinations, and 45% faster verification.
